Vātulaśuddhāgama
------------------------------------------
The आगमस् are subsidiary scriptures deemed as apauruṣeya (not man-made but revealed by God Himself) by their votaries.
They are classified into three main groups: शैवागमस्, शाक्तागमस् or तन्त्रस् and Vaiṣṇavāgamas.
There are 28 शैवागमस् considered प्रधान (main) and 225 as upāgamas (secondary).
The Vātulaśuddhāgama is classified among the 18 शैवागमस् known as Rudrabheda.
The work has 778 verses distributed among ten paṭalas or chapters. It is in the form of a dialogue between स्कन्द (Subrahmaṇya) and his ड़थेर् शिव.
Sometimes eleven additional chapters are added as an anubandha or appendix.
There is an old commentary in Sanskrit but it is incomplete.
One Mallaṇṇa of Gubbi (in the Karnataka State) wrote a detailed commentary in Kannada in A. D. 1475.
A brief account of the work may now be given.
1. Tattvabhedapaṭala (150 verses)
Tattva or the highest truth is classified into three types: शिव, सदाशिव and Maheśa. Śivatattva is niṣkala (without parts). Sadāśivatattva is niṣkala and sakala, hence has both parts and is partless. Maheśatattva is sakala (with parts).
After describing their characteristics, the five śaktis or powers that evolve out of शिव, viz, parā (the highest), ādi (primeval), icchā (volition), ज्ञान (know-ledge) and kriyā (action) are recounted.
This is followed by a detailed account of सृष्टि or च्रेअतिओन्.
There is also a description of the various लीलामूर्तिस् or forms of शिव such as Somadhārī, Bhikṣāṭanamūrti, Kāmāri and those of the Śaktis (goddesses) such as Umā, अम्बिका, Īśvarī, मनोन्मनी and others.
2. Varṇabheda Paṭala (81 verses)
Hara (Śiva or God) is Śabdabrahma. He is the personification of all sounds and varṇas (letters of the alphabet) which form his body. Details of these varṇas are given in the rest of the chapter, along with the deities that preside over them, which knowledge is necessary to understand the mantras properly.
3. Cakrabheda Paṭala (42 verses)
Cakras are geometrical figures representing certain deities. If properly drawn, they will exude the power of the respective deity. This chapter deals with all the details connected with the चक्रस् such as a suitable place to draw them, their proportion and methods of drawing, details of petals and circles, colours to be used, placement of deities and so on.
Worship of properly drawn चक्रस् can fulfil all desires.
4. Vargabheda Paṭala (46 verses)
It begins with a classification of the varṇas or letters of the alphabet into several vargas or groups. This is followed by some details regarding mantras and bījas (seed-letters).
5. Mantrabheda Paṭala (107 verses)
The origin and nature of mantras, their meaning and utility are described here. Some ritualistic details like the making of a मण्डप and drawing of the चक्रस् (geometrical figures) as also the placement of bījākṣaras are given.
Then there is a detailed description of certain mantras of शिव, called prāsāda mantras, their varieties and uses.
6. Praṇavabheda Paṭala (27 verses)
This short section deals mainly with प्रणव or ओङ्कार, its nature, method of meditation and the associated deities.
This is followed by a delineation of its पञ्चभेदस् or five varieties.
7. Brahmabheda Paṭala (76 verses)
This deals with 25 aspects of Sakala-ब्रह्मन् (with attributes) and five more of Niṣkala-ब्रह्मन् (without attributes). The latter are: सद्योजात, वामदेव, अघोर, Tatpuruṣa and ईश्वर. Their relation with प्रणव (Oṅkāra) and modes of meditation are also discussed.
8. Aṅgabheda Paṭala (104 verses)
The aṅgas or limbs of the body are divided into six groups: śivāṅga, bhūtāṅga, kūṭāṅga, vidyāṅga, śaktyaṅga and sāmānyāṅga. The mantras associated with them are described in detail.
9. Mantrajāta Paṭala (82 verses)
After declaring that शिवलिङ्ग is mantramaya (consisting of mantras), 19 varieties of mantranāmas or mantras of शिव, with different names such as atibāla, sabāla and kaumāra are described.
10. Mantrakīla Paṭala (63 verses)
This chapter deals with the mantras to be adopted as also the ones to be rejected, the right way of pronouncing them, the nature of mantras and other topics connected with rituals.
Most of the printed texts add a long appendix comprising eleven topics that include the following:
Prāyaścittas (expiations); ceremonial preparation of पञ्चगव्य (five products derived from a cow); होम; celebration of the festival of शिव in a temple; method of establishing the शिवलिङ्ग; rites associated with it or with other deities like गणपति or विष्णु or देवी to be performed for one to nine nights.
These are taken from various other works.

vātsalyabhāva
------------------------------------------
This is one of the several types of भक्ति or devotion. It is the love of a devotee towards God as that of a मोथेर् towards her child. यशोदा’s love for the child कृष्ण and कौसल्या’s towards the child राम are classic examples.
The love of a devotee towards God as that of a child towards its मोथेर् can also be grouped under this category. रामकृष्ण परमहṁस (A. D. 1836-1886) retained this attitude towards मोथेर् Kālī till the end.
